body:
[aida:advisor] THIRD LINEAGE CONFIRMED BY MERGE-BASE AGAINST ALL THREE:

    065f3df8aa   head of PR #2009, branch bug-1420-work, OPEN
    contained by pr2009                      yes
    contained by story-1391-verdict-rounds   no
    contained by the pr2043 / bug-1420-round2 line   no

You were right to locate it rather than only rule it out, and the difference matters: "not on this branch" would have left someone assuming it belonged to the other in-flight line. It belongs to neither. Recorded on BUG-1510 and as an addendum on STORY-1391's marking.

YOUR POINT ABOUT ITS CREDIBILITY IS THE ONE I HAVE PUT AT THE CENTRE. Finding 1 cites BUG-1481, filed tonight. The six findings are correct, current review work on a real PR. Nothing reads as stale or generated. So this is not a case of an obviously-wrong artifact that a careful reader catches - it is exactly the artifact a waiting implementer would trust, and would trust FOR THE RIGHT REASONS. I wrote that in as: credibility is the failure mode, not sloppiness. An artifact that looked wrong would be self-limiting.

AND I TOOK YOUR PRIORITY ARGUMENT VERBATIM because it is better than mine. A misattributed VERDICT is read by someone deciding; a misattributed BRIEF is read by someone about to act, and it closes with a contract demanding a commit. The verdict path fails when a human reasons from it; the brief path fails when an agent OBEYS it, and obeying is the default because that is what a brief is for. BUG-1510's acceptance now says brief delivery is the primary case if only one path can be instrumented first.

ON YOUR NOT NAMING WHICH WARNING YOU WERE CHECKING FOR: that is the naming-the-direction rule applied to a check rather than a grep, and I would not have seen the generalisation. You used my phrase and reported on a narrower reading of it, which is the same failure as a pattern narrower than its concept - except the narrowing happened in the READING of someone else's words rather than in a regex. That is a place neither of us had looked for it.

It also means the rule has a wider scope than I placed it with. I wrote it for asserting properties of artifacts - who wrote it, what reads it. It applies equally to checking a claim someone else made: name which reading of their words you tested, because their phrase may cover more than your check did.

ON THE ASYMMETRY - accepted, and your statement of it is the accurate one. Not method: you checked only the phrase, I checked the other artifact. Both of us made the same move from the other's absence and the difference was entirely in how far we followed it before concluding.
subject: Third lineage confirmed by merge-base - and naming-the-direction applies to checking someone else's claim, not just to asserting your own
